one_line_contribution: On a synthetically relocated ALFWorld it manipulates the scope at which object-receptacle bindings hold (one rule per class, per (scene,class), or per game) and the rate at which an eval game's own expert trajectory is planted in the bank, then asks at each scope whether a rule-written static prefix (a sentence, a table, or nothing) matches top-k retrieval and how much of the retrieval residual over the best static arm is replay of the game's own near-duplicate.
closest_prior_work: EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421, verified via s2cli paper, S2 channel, 2026-05-18, 7 citations): it organizes agent memory along a memory-scope axis (in-episode vs cross-episode) crossed with content, and reports that long-context baselines still outperform specialized memory methods. That is the same headline shape as the whole-bank arm here, and it pre-empts the 'does a query buy anything over the bank in context' half of the contribution; it does not manipulate binding scope, does not vary duplicate rate, and has no compiled static arm, so it does not scoop the ladder itself. Two other verified threats: The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified, S2) already gives a trajectory-level account of agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory with compounding errors and weak recovery - P6(b) is close to a single-cell replication of that mechanism on ALFWorld with the correct duplicate pinned at rank 1, and the proposal predicts the null direction without engaging the prior evidence that points the other way. ExecRetrieval (arXiv:2609.01865, verified, S2, 2026-09-01) is the closest methodological neighbour to the planting design: it plants execution-verified single-edit near-clone distractors of each query's canonical item in the retrieval pool to measure whether embeddings discriminate correct from near-clone-but-wrong - the same 'construct the pool so the near-duplicate is controlled' move, in code retrieval rather than agent memory and scored on retrieval, not task success. Finally, the conceptual claim 'near-duplicate overlap inflates a measured gain' is owned by the dedup/contamination literature the proposal itself cites (2107.06499 verified, HF); transposing it to experience banks is a real but incremental step.
strongest_objection: The ladder's results are largely fixed by the construction, not measured. The scope taxonomy is the experimenter's own relocation rule, so 'the smallest static substitute grows with binding scope' is an information-theoretic consequence of how the three worlds were built: under a global relocation rule one sentence is a sufficient statistic of the bank; under a scene rule the (scene,class) table is; under a per-game rule nothing short of per-instance rows is. What remains empirical is only the narrow reader-consumption question of whether Qwen3-32B applies a stated rule as well as it applies a shown trajectory (P2, P4) and whether it replays its own expert trajectory (P5, which is a positive control dressed as a prediction). The headline is weaker still: at instance scope another game's duplicate carries zero information about this game by construction, so P6(a)'s no-spillover is near-entailed (the automated check agrees), and its only falsifying channel - generic search-strategy transfer - is never isolated by a bank-composition control; worse, adding foreign duplicates can only displace informative same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, which pushes N(0.5) down and thus away from the falsifier. And the title's quantity - how much of a memory gain is near-duplicate leakage - is never measured on any bank that was not built to contain the answer: natural ALFWorld is class-scope with no instance duplicates, gets exactly one anchor cell (P0), and every leakage number in the paper comes from duplicates the experimenter planted at a rate the experimenter chose. A second, sharper technical objection: the +14 and +28 margins are absolute net points inherited from the natural bank (k0 = 0.54, k3 = 0.81-0.87), but relocation plus a 25-step budget changes the base rate and the headroom in each scope, and no per-scope normalization or base-rate check is specified, so P5 can be falsified for ceiling reasons and the three rungs of the ladder are not on comparable scales.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Run the instance-scope row table you declined: a cached static prefix of one binding row per eval game (<= 274 rows, ~3k tokens, the same size as the scene-scope table you do run) plus a per-game one-line binding prefix. That turns 'no static substitute exists at instance scope' from a definition into a measurement, and it separates 'the duplicate's value is one bit of binding information' from 'the duplicate's value is trajectory replay' - the actual scientific question at that rung. If the reader finds its own row among 274, P7 and the headline collapse, which is exactly what a confirmatory design should risk. (2) Add the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size and rank-1/2/3 composition fixed and swap other games' exact duplicates for matched non-duplicate same-scene trajectories, with a dose at s = 0.25/0.75, so the strategy-transfer channel is shown to exist before its absence is claimed. (3) Re-anchor margins per scope: measure k0 and static3-relocated in each relocated world first, pre-register margins as fractions of that scope's own headroom, and report the ceiling. (4) Put one leakage number on an unmanipulated bank - delete (goal text, scene) near-duplicates from the natural train bank and re-run k3 - so the title's claim touches a bank nobody constructed for it. (5) State a family-wise plan: eight pre-registered predictions over 22-25 cells at two seeds, several of them equivalence tests at margin 8 with ~5-net half-widths, needs a multiplicity policy. (6) Cite and engage arXiv:2604.27003 (When Continual Learning Moves to Memory), which my search returned and the related work misses.
missing_baseline: The instance-scope binding-row arm - a cached per-game one-line static prefix naming the game's own class-receptacle binding, and its query-free counterpart, the <= 274-row instance table. The proposal defines this away ('the instance-scope static substitute is a prefix whose size does not grow with the number of instances; the O(instances) duplicate-row table is the whole-bank arm in row form and is not run'), but the row table is ~3k tokens and fits context, unlike the 80-trajectory whole-bank arm at ~11k, and it is the same artifact class as the <= 274-row table that IS run at scene scope; the asymmetry is what makes P7 look confirmed. Second omission: a rank-1 content control at instance scope (duplicate replaced by a matched non-duplicate same-class, same-scene trajectory at fixed bank size and token count), without which the s-manipulation confounds 'the duplicate' with 'bank composition at ranks 1-3'. Third, minor: a random-3 same-scene retrieval placebo at instance scope; blind1's -3 net bounds a wrong-type length effect on the natural bank, not a same-scene random draw in the relocated world.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round - four query classes with IDs, both channels named, two verifications - and it survives auditing: I verified every ID its novelty argument rests on through channel (a) (s2cli, S2+HF), and all resolved with matching content: 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (S2, memory scope = in-episode vs cross-episode, exactly as the proposal characterizes it), 2606.02461 AgentCL (HF), 2511.20857 Evo-Memory (S2, 123 cits), 2512.10696 = 'Remember Me, Refine Me' / ReMe (S2, ACL, 55 cits), 2607.10608 Compliance Trap (S2), 2602.08316 SWE Context Bench (S2, 10 cits), 2107.06499 Deduplicating Training Data (HF). I could not check 2411.03923 or 2311.04850 (home-literature citations, not load-bearing for novelty) - unverified. My own searches, all answered by channel (a); channel (b) WebSearch is unavailable in this session and was not used: (Q1, --recent) 'near-duplicate leakage agent experience memory retrieval gain duplicate rate' -> 12 hits, nearest 2607.10608, 2606.02461, 2606.24595, and one item the proposal does not cite, 2604.27003 (When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: experience reuse in LLM agents, memory design trades transfer against forgetting); none manipulates duplicate rate. (Q2) 'compiled static prompt matches retrieval agent experience memory ALFWorld exemplars' -> 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2605.05413 From History to State, 2605.20616 Auto-Dreamer, 2606.06087 LatentSkill, 2505.00234 self-generated in-context examples; none reports retrieval minus a compiled static arm as a function of binding scope. (Q3, closest named method) 'EvoMemBench memory scope benchmark long-context baseline outperforms memory methods' -> 2605.18421 (verified), plus 2606.13681 EvoArena; confirms the scope framing exists but at a different axis. (Q4, --recent) 'controlled duplicate rate planted identical task trajectory bank measures how much memory gain is leakage' -> effectively empty on the mechanism (Omega-S, HiMPO, 2606.10229 demonstration-curation metrics); reported as empty, not as evidence. (Q5) 'object receptacle location binding household embodied agent memory generalizes across scenes instance specific' -> MEMENTO 2505.16348 (verified, S2, 12 cits: episodic memory gives personalized knowledge plus in-context learning benefit in embodied personalization) and KARMA 2409.14908, CAPEAM 2308.07241; none manipulates binding scope. Weaknesses of the proposal's check that I would flag: it runs no query in the pool-construction vocabulary that would surface ExecRetrieval 2609.01865 (verified, 2026-09-01, planted execution-verified near-clone distractors per query - the same methodological move, in code retrieval), and none in the embodied/household-memory vocabulary where instance bindings actually live (MEMENTO); its negatives are abstract-level only, which is worth stating explicitly rather than as 'no collision found'.
